title: Closed shop and single union agreement

blocks.heading: Closed shop and single union agreement
blocks.text: In the closed-shop syllabus model, all employees must be members of the trade union. A single union agreement means the firm deals with one particular union for representation and bargaining. One concerns required membership; the other concerns which union the employer recognises or deals with. A statement that management bargains with one union does not by itself state that every worker must belong to it. These definitions describe organisational arrangements, not a claim that a particular requirement is currently lawful or enforceable in every place. Use the facts of the arrangement rather than treating the terms as interchangeable.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Assume Ota Tools deals with one specified union, while a different workplace expressly requires union membership for all employees. The first describes a single union agreement; the second supplies the defining closed-shop condition. The first alone does not prove compulsory membership.

blocks.heading: Closed shop
blocks.text: A closed shop is an arrangement in which all employees must be members of the trade union. The defining feature is required membership, not simply that a union exists or negotiates. This is the syllabus model, not an assertion about current enforceability in a particular workplace. A single union agreement concerns the union the employer deals with and does not on its own establish compulsory membership.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Assume a workplace expressly requires membership for all employees. That stated membership condition identifies the closed-shop model. The business name or workforce size does not do so.

blocks.heading: Single union agreement
blocks.text: A single union agreement means a firm deals with one particular trade union for representation or bargaining rather than multiple competing unions. It can simplify discussion and reduce conflicting claims, but it can leave concerns about how different workers are represented. It differs from compulsory membership: recognition of one bargaining union does not by itself tell us that every employee belongs.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An employer agrees to conduct its bargaining with one specified union. The recognition arrangement is the key fact. Without a membership requirement, it cannot be treated as evidence of a closed shop.
